author: BBC News
description:
Israel’s general election is too close to call, as exit polls suggest that Gadi Eisenkot’s bloc has won the most seats, ahead of Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party.

Eisenkot leads the newly formed Yashar party and is the main figure in the "change bloc", a group of opposition parties with the shared goal of ousting Benjamin Netanyahu from power. 

Israeli elections can be decided by just a handful of seats, the exit polls have not always been reliable and counting the votes may take several days. 

All 120 seats in the Knesset, Israel's parliament, are up for grabs, but no party has won an overall majority in the past and governments have been made up of coalitions.

It’s Israel's first legislative election since the Hamas-led attacks on 7 October 2023 and the issue of Israel’s security has dominated the campaign.

description:
A truce has begun in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, where residents have been trapped without food, water and electricity.

Ukrainian officials and Russia's defence ministry say the limited ceasefire is being respected. The truce, which the White House said was secured by US First Lady Melania Trump, is meant to allow aid deliveries and a civilian evacuation on Friday.

But some residents have told the BBC there are concerns the ceasefire will not hold.

The current truce is supposed to allow supplies in and enable roads to be cleared of mines to allow people safe passage out in an evacuation planned to take place on Friday.

Nine women have been paid compensation following claims a police force failed to investigate serving and former officers for domestic abuse and sexual violence.
 
The women say they were not taken seriously when they reported alleged cases of rape, assault and coercive control by male officers employed by Devon and Cornwall Police.
 
One woman described the force as a "big boys' club" which had "protected" the man who she claims assaulted her.
 
The force has apologised to the women and agreed an out-of-court settlement to pay compensation without admitting legal liability.
 
If you have been affected by any of the issues in this story, help and support is available at BBC Action Line.

description:
US federal prosecutors have taken steps to charge ex-Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director James Comey with leaking national defence information, according to a court filing.
 
It marks the third time the justice department has moved to bring criminal charges against Comey, a long-time critic of US President Donald Trump.
 
Few details are provided about the two counts in the three-page filing, but Comey's lawyers said in separate court papers that the case stemmed from an alleged disclosure of classified information to the New York Times in October 2016, while he was head of the FBI.
 
Comey denied any wrongdoing in a video posted on Substack on Monday, calling the charges an "appalling abuse".
